rows: Severe thunderstorm winds struck from west of Carrizo Springs into Maverick County. As the storms moved southward, they knocked over trees and blew down power lines from west of Carrizo Springs to El Indio and southward to the Aerostat site. The wind damage was most severe in the…
The Maverick County Sheriff's Department reported that some vehicles had been damaged by the large hail in the Quemado area.

A supercell thunderstorm formed in the Mexican mountains west of Piedras Negras, across the Rio Grande from Eagle Pass. Reports from west of the Rio Grande indicate that a large and devastating tornado stuck Piedras Negras from the west, then dissipated on the west side of the Ri…
Hail was reported at the Maverick County airport.
Windows blown out in the Chula Vista Area 6 to 10 miles southeast of Eagle Pass.
Trees were also reported blown down.
There were power outages in Eagle Pass associated with thunderstorm wind damage.
Power lines were reported down between Eagle Pass and La Pryor on Highway 57.
The El Indio Co-op Observer reported nickel size hail at the Cage Ranch.
A thunderstorms produced quarter size hail in the Elm Creek area north of Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 50 mph that blew down numerous trees, power lines, light poles, and street signs in Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 45 mph that broke several 3-4 inch diameter tree branches.
Golfball sized hail in Elm Creek was reported via Twitter. Time of occurrence was estimated via radar.
A thunderstorm produced half dollar size hail on FM1021 southeast of Eagle Pass.
Three-quarter inch hail was reported by a storm chaser in the city of El Indio.
One inch diameter hail was reported by a storm chaser in the city of El Indio.
One inch diameter hail was reported along highway 277 between Quemado and Elm Creek.
Border patrol in Quemado reported quarter sized hail.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that blew down many large tree limbs.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that knocked down power lines approximately two miles south of FM1665 and Hwy 277 between Quemado and Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced golf ball size hail in Quemado.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that downed power lines in Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 65 mph that knocked down power lines near the intersection of Hwy 277 and Hwy 131 northwest of Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that knocked down a few large mesquite trees along Hwy 277 just north of Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced a wind gust measured at 50 kts. by the AWOS at the Maverick County Memorial International Airport.

A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 80 mph. Power lines were blown down at Ave. B and Del Rio Blvd. in Eagle Pass. There was a roof blown off a house and onto a car in the 900 block of Ave C.
A thunderstorm produced ping pong ball size hail in Elm Creek.
A thunderstorm produced golf ball size hail north of Eagle Pass. The report was from a picture on Twitter.
A thunderstorm produced nickel size hail at Radar Base. The report was from social media.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 85 mph that blew off part of an awning from a building near downtown Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that knocked down power poles near the intersection of Cleveland St. and Jefferson St. in Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph. These winds damaged two roofs and downed power lines in El Indio.
A thunderstorm produced a wind gust measured at 62 mph and nickel size hail south of El Indio.
A thunderstorm produced nickel size hail and a wind gust measured at 62 mph south of El Indio.
A thunderstorm produced nickel size hail in Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts measured at 50 kts by the AWOS at Maverick County Memorial International Airport outside Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced golf ball size hail in Eagle Pass.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that knocked down tree limbs and caused power outages in Eagle Pass.
